title: 1992 AHSME Problem 22
statement: Ten points are selected on the positive \(x\)-axis, \(\mathrm{X}^+,\) and five points are selected on the positive \(y\)-axis, \(\mathrm{Y}^+.\) The fifty segments connecting the ten selected points on \(\mathrm{X}^+\) to the five selected points on \(\mathrm{Y}^+\) are drawn. What is the maximum possible number of points of intersection of these fifty segments that could lie in the interior of the first quadrant?

solutions.text:
Choose two of the \(10\) points on the \(x\)-axis and two of the \(5\) points on the \(y\)-axis. Among the four connecting segments, the two with reversed endpoint order cross exactly once. The points can be chosen so no three segments meet at one interior point, so the maximum is \[ \binom{10}{2}\binom{5}{2}=45\cdot10=450. \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: An interior crossing is determined by choosing two points from each axis
For each selected pair on each axis, exactly one pair of the four connecting segments crosses
